metadata.case_name: CHIU TAK SANG v. KWAN HON LAM

injuries.description: compound dislocation of the right subtalar joint
source: the injury suffered by the Plaintiff was a compound dislocation of the right subtalar joint, which is located between the heel bone and the shin bone.

injuries.description: quite advanced post traumatic osteo-arthritis of the (right) subtalar joint (joint cartilage badly worn to the extent that it is now almost bone rubbing on bone)
source: X-ray examination in October this year showed that the Plaintiff has developed quite advanced post traumatic osteo-arthritis. The joint cartilage has been badly worn to the extent that it is now almost bone rubbing on bone.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: pain when walking or lifting heavy objects
incapable of doing strenuous labouring work (not possible to return to work before the accident as a lorry attendant)
sacrifice of mobility (fusion operation will free him of pain but with the sacrifice of mobility)

losses.description: Impairment of right subtalar joint with advanced post traumatic osteo-arthritis (joint cartilage badly worn, almost bone on bone).
Pain on walking or lifting heavy objects and eventual sacrifice of mobility if fusion operation undertaken.
Incapable of doing strenuous labouring work and not able to return to pre-accident work as a lorry attendant.

comparable_cases.injury_description: a disability which mars general activities and enjoyment of life but allows reasonable mobility to the victim for example ... bad fractures leaving recurrent pain
